title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 14. The Favour to Gauridasa during the Pastimes in Navadvipa after the Journey to Vrindavana
html:
The Lord comes to Kuliya, and the people of Navadvipa beg Him to return; Shachi welcomes and feeds her son; praise of Gauranga and Nityananda; the Lord leaves His Deity with Vishnupriya and sports with Gadadhara, Srivasa and Shridhara; in the house of Gauridasa Pandita, Gaura and Nityananda manifest Themselves as Deities, eternal like all the Lord's forms

Verse 1

एवं क्रमेण पथि गौरचन्द्रश्चलन् समायात् कुलियाह्वपुरम्।
श्रुत्वा ययुस्तत्र महानिधेः किल श्रीमन्नवद्वीपनिवासिनः परे॥१॥

evaṁ krameṇa pathi gauracandraścalan samāyāt kuliyāhvapuram|
śrutvā yayustatra mahānidheḥ kila śrīmannavadvīpanivāsinaḥ pare||1||

evam — thus; kramena — by stages; pathi — on the road; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; chalan — travelling; samayat — arrived; kuliya-ahva-puram — at the town called Kuliya; shrutva — hearing; yayuh — went; tatra — there; maha-nidheh — of the great treasure; kila — indeed; shrimat-navadvipa-nivasinah — the dwellers of glorious Navadvipa; pare — the others.

1Thus, travelling the road stage by stage, Gaurachandra came to the town called Kuliya1. Hearing of the great treasure, the rest of the people of glorious Navadvipa went there too.

Verse 2

दृष्ट्वा प्रभोः श्रीमुखपङ्कजं मुहुः पिबन्ति हर्षेण न तृप्तिमापिरे।
वदन्ति सर्वे कृतकण्ठवाससो जगद्गुरुं स्नेहवशं तमीश्वरम्॥२॥

dṛṣṭvā prabhoḥ śrīmukhapaṅkajaṁ muhuḥ pibanti harṣeṇa na tṛptimāpire|
vadanti sarve kṛtakaṇṭhavāsaso jagadguruṁ snehavaśaṁ tamīśvaram||2||

drishtva — seeing; prabhoh — of the Lord; shri-mukha-pankajam — the lovely lotus face; muhuh — again and again; pibanti — they drink; harshena — with joy; na — not; triptim — satiety; apire — reached; vadanti — say; sarve — all; krita-kantha-vasasah — with their cloths about their necks; jagat-gurum — to the Teacher of the world; sneha-vasham — subject to love; tam — that; ishvaram — Lord.

2Seeing the lovely lotus of the Lord's face, they drank it in with joy again and again, yet could not be sated. With their cloths about their necks2, they all said to the Lord, the Teacher of the world, who is subject to love:

Verse 3

श्रीमन्नवद्वीपमलङ्कुरु प्रभो संकीर्तनानन्दसुमग्नचित्तैः।
स्वभक्तवर्गैरिति प्रार्थितः स्वयं हरिर्ययौ तत्र स्वनामकौतुकी॥३॥

śrīmannavadvīpamalaṅkuru prabho saṁkīrtanānandasumagnacittaiḥ|
svabhaktavargairiti prārthitaḥ svayaṁ hariryayau tatra svanāmakautukī||3||

shrimat-navadvipam — glorious Navadvipa; alankuru — adorn; prabho — O Lord; sankirtana-ananda-su-magna-chittaih — whose hearts were deeply immersed in the bliss of sankirtana; sva-bhakta-vargaih — by His devotees; iti — thus; prarthitah — entreated; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; yayau — went; tatra — there; sva-nama-kautuki — delighting in His own names.

3"O Lord, grace glorious Navadvipa with Your presence!" Entreated thus by His devotees, whose hearts were immersed in the bliss of sankirtana, Hari Himself, who delights in His own names, went there.

Verse 4

आगत्य मातुश्चरणाभिवन्दनं भूमौ निपत्य कृतवान् मातृभक्तः।
तदैव सा सत्वरमेव हर्षाद् विस्मृत्य सर्वं च तमालिलिङ्ग॥४॥

āgatya mātuścaraṇābhivandanaṁ bhūmau nipatya kṛtavān mātṛbhaktaḥ|
tadaiva sā satvarameva harṣād vismṛtya sarvaṁ ca tamāliliṅga||4||

agatya — arriving; matuh — to His mother; charana-abhivandanam — obeisance at the feet; bhumau — to the ground; nipatya — falling; kritavan — made; matri-bhaktah — devoted to His mother; tada — then; eva — at once; sa — she; satvaram — quickly; eva — indeed; harshat — out of joy; vismritya — forgetting; sarvam — everything; cha — and; tam — Him; alilinga — embraced.

4On arriving, He who was devoted to His mother fell to the ground and bowed at her feet; and at once, forgetting everything in her joy, she hastily embraced Him.

Verse 5

सा चुम्बती कृष्णमुखारविन्दं सिषेच तं वत्सलभक्तिनीरैः।
चतुर्विधेनापि रसेन चान्नं सम्भोजयित्वा मुदमाप वत्सला॥५॥

sā cumbatī kṛṣṇamukhāravindaṁ siṣeca taṁ vatsalabhaktinīraiḥ|
caturvidhenāpi rasena cānnaṁ sambhojayitvā mudamāpa vatsalā||5||

sa — she; chumbati — kissing; krishna-mukha-aravindam — Krishna's lotus face; sishecha — bathed; tam — Him; vatsala-bhakti-niraih — with the waters of maternal love; chatur-vidhena — of four kinds; api — also; rasena — with taste; cha — and; annam — food; sambhojayitva — feeding; mudam — joy; apa — obtained; vatsala — the loving mother.

5Kissing Krishna's lotus face, she bathed Him in the waters of maternal love; and when she had fed Him food of the four kinds3, the loving mother was filled with joy.

Verse 6

नित्यानन्देन सार्धं सकलरसगुरुः श्रीलगौराङ्गचन्द्रो
मात्रा दत्तं परममधुरमन्नमाद्यं च सायम्।
भुक्त्वा वत्सलभक्तिपूर्णतमया बद्धस्तया श्रीहरि-
र्मात्रा सर्वसुखप्रदो जयति स श्रीभक्तवश्यः प्रभुः॥६॥

nityānandena sārdhaṁ sakalarasaguruḥ śrīlagaurāṅgacandro
mātrā dattaṁ paramamadhuramannamādyaṁ ca sāyam|
bhuktvā vatsalabhaktipūrṇatamayā baddhastayā śrīhari-
rmātrā sarvasukhaprado jayati sa śrībhaktavaśyaḥ prabhuḥ||6||

nityanandena — Nityananda; sardham — with; sakala-rasa-guruh — the teacher of every rasa; shrila-gauranga-chandrah — Shrila Gaurangachandra; matra — by His mother; dattam — given; parama-madhuram — most sweet; annam — food; adyam — choice; cha — and; sayam — in the evening; bhuktva — having eaten; vatsala-bhakti-purnatamaya — utterly full of maternal love; baddhah — bound; taya — by her; shri-harih — Sri Hari; matra — by the mother; sarva-sukha-pradah — giver of every joy; jayati — glory to; sah — that; shri-bhakta-vashyah — subject to His devotees; prabhuh — Lord.

6In the evening, together with Nityananda, Srila Gaurangachandra, the teacher of every rasa, ate the sweetest, choicest food His mother had given Him. Glory to the Lord Sri Hari, the giver of every joy, who is subject to His devotees — He whom His mother had bound with her brimming love!

Verse 7

नित्यानन्दो जयति सततं गौरप्रेमाभिमत्तः
सान्द्रानन्दोज्ज्वलमयनवद्वीपमालम्बमानः।
नानाभावैः प्रणयिनिकरैः सेव्यमानो निजेशं
तन्नामामृतकीर्तनैस्त्रिजगतां तापत्रयं नाशयन्॥७॥

nityānando jayati satataṁ gaurapremābhimattaḥ
sāndrānandojjvalamayanavadvīpamālambamānaḥ|
nānābhāvaiḥ praṇayinikaraiḥ sevyamāno nijeśaṁ
tannāmāmṛtakīrtanaistrijagatāṁ tāpatrayaṁ nāśayan||7||

nityanandah — Nityananda; jayati — glory to; satatam — ever; gaura-prema-abhimattah — intoxicated with love for Gaura; sandra-ananda-ujjvala-maya-navadvipam — Navadvipa, radiant with dense bliss; alambamanah — taking as his support; nana-bhavaih — in various moods; pranayi-nikaraih — with hosts of loving devotees; sevyamanah — serving; nija-isham — his own Lord; tat-nama-amrita-kirtanaih — by kirtanas of the nectar of His name; tri-jagatam — of the three worlds; tapa-trayam — the threefold misery; nashayan — destroying.

7Glory for ever to Nityananda, intoxicated with love for Gaura! Taking Navadvipa, radiant with dense bliss, as His refuge, He serves His own Lord with hosts of loving devotees in their various moods, and with kirtanas of the nectar of His name destroys the threefold misery of the three worlds.

Verse 8

प्रकाशरूपेण निजप्रियायाः समीपमासाद्य निजां हि मूर्तिम्।
विधाय तस्यां स्थित एष कृष्णः सा लक्ष्मीरूपा च निषेवते प्रभुम्॥८॥

prakāśarūpeṇa nijapriyāyāḥ samīpamāsādya nijāṁ hi mūrtim|
vidhāya tasyāṁ sthita eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ sā lakṣmīrūpā ca niṣevate prabhum||8||

prakasha-rupena — in a manifest form; nija-priyayah — of His beloved; samipam — near; asadya — coming; nijam — His own; hi — indeed; murtim — Deity form; vidhaya — manifesting; tasyam — in it; sthitah — abides; eshah — this; krishnah — Krishna; sa — she; lakshmi-rupa — Lakshmi in nature; cha — and; nishevate — serves; prabhum — the Lord.

8Coming in a prakasha form4 to His beloved, Krishna manifested His Deity form and abides in it; and she, Lakshmi herself, serves the Lord5.

Verse 9

गदाधरेणापि समं रसज्ञो गौराङ्गचन्द्रो विहरत्यहर्निशम्।
श्रीमन्नवद्वीपनिवासिभिः सह श्रीकृष्णसंकीर्तनमग्नचित्तैः॥९॥

gadādhareṇāpi samaṁ rasajño gaurāṅgacandro viharatyaharniśam|
śrīmannavadvīpanivāsibhiḥ saha śrīkṛṣṇasaṁkīrtanamagnacittaiḥ||9||

gadadharena — Gadadhara; api — also; samam — with; rasa-jnah — the knower of rasa; gauranga-chandrah — Gaurangachandra; viharati — sports; ahar-nisham — day and night; shrimat-navadvipa-nivasibhih — the dwellers of glorious Navadvipa; saha — with; shri-krishna-sankirtana-magna-chittaih — whose hearts are immersed in the sankirtana of Sri Krishna.

9And together with Gadadhara, Gaurangachandra, the knower of rasa, sports day and night with the people of glorious Navadvipa, whose hearts are immersed in the sankirtana of Sri Krishna.

Verse 10

श्रीवासमुख्या ये भक्तास्तेषां गृहे गृहे प्रभुः।
स्वप्रकाशतया पूर्णकीर्तनानन्ददायकः॥१०॥

śrīvāsamukhyā ye bhaktāsteṣāṁ gṛhe gṛhe prabhuḥ|
svaprakāśatayā pūrṇakīrtanānandadāyakaḥ||10||

shrivasa-mukhyah — headed by Srivasa; ye — who; bhaktah — devotees; tesham — their; grihe grihe — in house after house; prabhuh — the Lord; sva-prakashataya — by His self-manifestation; purna-kirtana-ananda-dayakah — giving the full bliss of kirtana.

10In every house of the devotees headed by Srivasa the Lord, manifesting Himself, bestows the full bliss of kirtana.

Verse 11

विद्याविनोदलोलाद्यैः सम्पूर्णः कौतुकादिभिः।
श्रीधरेण समं नित्यं क्रीडति गौरसुन्दरः॥११॥

vidyāvinodalolādyaiḥ sampūrṇaḥ kautukādibhiḥ|
śrīdhareṇa samaṁ nityaṁ krīḍati gaurasundaraḥ||11||

vidya-vinoda-lola-adyaih — with eagerness for learned amusements and the like; sampurnah — full; kautuka-adibhih — of jests and the like; shridharena — Shridhara; samam — with; nityam — constantly; kridati — frolics; gaura-sundarah — Gaurasundara.

11Full of eagerness for learned amusements, jests and the like, Gaurasundara constantly frolics with Shridhara6.

Verse 12

ततो नित्यानन्दगौरचन्द्रौ सर्वेश्वरेश्वरौ।
जयतां गौरीदासाख्यपण्डितस्य गृहे प्रभू॥१२॥

tato nityānandagauracandrau sarveśvareśvarau|
jayatāṁ gaurīdāsākhyapaṇḍitasya gṛhe prabhū||12||

tatah — then; nityananda-gaurachandrau — Nityananda and Gaurachandra; sarva-ishvara-ishvarau — the Lords of the lords of all; jayatam — glory to them; gauridasa-akhya-panditasya — of the pandita named Gauridasa; grihe — in the house; prabhu — the two Lords.

12Then — glory to Them! — Nityananda and Gaurachandra, the two Lords, the Lords of the lords of all, came to the house of the pandita named Gauridasa7.

Verse 13

तस्य प्रेम्णा निबद्धौ तौ प्रकाश्य रुचिरां शुभाम्।
मूर्तिं स्वां स्वां रसैः पूर्णां सर्वशक्तिसमन्विताम्॥१३॥

tasya premṇā nibaddhau tau prakāśya rucirāṁ śubhām|
mūrtiṁ svāṁ svāṁ rasaiḥ pūrṇāṁ sarvaśaktisamanvitām||13||

tasya — his; premna — by the love; nibaddhau — bound; tau — the two; prakashya — manifesting; ruchiram — lovely; shubham — auspicious; murtim — Deity; svam svam — each his own; rasaih — with rasas; purnam — full; sarva-shakti-samanvitam — endowed with every power.

13Bound by his love, They each manifested a lovely, auspicious Deity of Themselves, full of Their own rasas and endowed with every power,

Verse 14

ददतुः परमप्रीतौ निवसन्तौ यथासुखम्।
ताभ्यां सह भुक्तवन्तावन्नं च विविधं रसम्॥१४॥

dadatuḥ paramaprītau nivasantau yathāsukham|
tābhyāṁ saha bhuktavantāvannaṁ ca vividhaṁ rasam||14||

dadatuh — they gave; parama-pritau — supremely pleased; nivasantau — dwelling; yatha-sukham — as they pleased; tabhyam — the two (Deities); saha — with; bhuktavantau — partook; annam — of food; cha — and; vividham — various; rasam — tastes.

14and in great delight gave Them to him; dwelling there as They pleased, They partook, together with those two Deities, of food of many tastes.

Verse 15

दृष्ट्वा द्वौ सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहौ द्विजसत्तमः।
शुद्धसख्यरसेनापि सेवयामास सर्वदा॥१५॥

dṛṣṭvā dvau saccidānandavigrahau dvijasattamaḥ|
śuddhasakhyarasenāpi sevayāmāsa sarvadā||15||

drishtva — seeing; dvau — the two; sat-chit-ananda-vigrahau — whose forms are being, consciousness and bliss; dvija-sattamah — the best of brahmanas; shuddha-sakhya-rasena — with the pure rasa of friendship; api — indeed; sevayam asa — served; sarvada — always.

15Seeing those two whose forms are being, consciousness and bliss, that best of brahmanas served Them always with the pure rasa of friendship.

Verse 16

सर्वे नित्याः शाश्वताश्च देहास्तस्य महात्मनः।
हानोपादानरहिता इति वेदानुसारतः॥१६॥

sarve nityāḥ śāśvatāśca dehāstasya mahātmanaḥ|
hānopādānarahitā iti vedānusārataḥ||16||

sarve — all; nityah — eternal; shashvatah — everlasting; cha — and; dehah — the bodies; tasya — of that; maha-atmanah — Supreme Soul; hana-upadana-rahitah — free from loss and gain; iti — thus; veda-anusaratah — according to the Vedas.

16All the bodies of the Supreme Soul are eternal and everlasting, subject neither to loss nor to gain — so the Vedas teach.

Verse 17

श्रीलीलाविग्रहाः सर्वे भक्तचित्ते निरन्तरम्।
तिष्ठन्ति परमानन्ददायिनो भक्तवत्सलाः॥१७॥

śrīlīlāvigrahāḥ sarve bhaktacitte nirantaram|
tiṣṭhanti paramānandadāyino bhaktavatsalāḥ||17||

shri-lila-vigrahah — the beautiful forms of His pastimes; sarve — all; bhakta-chitte — in the devotee's heart; nirantaram — unceasingly; tishthanti — abide; parama-ananda-dayinah — bestowing supreme bliss; bhakta-vatsalah — loving to the devotees.

17All the beautiful forms of His pastimes, bestowing supreme bliss and loving to the devotees, abide unceasingly in the devotee's heart.

Thus ends the fourteenth sarga, "The Favour to Gauridasa during the Pastimes in Navadvipa after the Journey to Vrindavana" (Shri-vrindavana-gamana-anantaram shri-navadvipa-vihare shri-gauridasa-anugraha), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Kuliya: a village on the bank of the Ganga opposite Navadvipa.
  2. A gesture of humble entreaty. The reading follows witness C; Haridasa Shastri's edition has "holding their cloths in their hands."
  3. That is, food that is chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
  4. Prakasha: the Lord's manifestation in several places at once in one and the same form.
  5. The beloved is Vishnupriya; the Deity is the form of the Lord which she served after He took sannyasa.
  6. Shridhara was a poor seller of banana leaves and fruit in Navadvipa with whom the Lord loved to banter.
  7. Gauridasa Pandita, an associate of the Lord from Ambika-Kalna; the Deities of Gaura and Nityananda spoken of next were worshipped in his house.
